doc.title: John Altman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 14, 2023

title: Orchestrating for Sakamoto and Elmer Bernstein
summary: Composers give differing material, from synth demos by Sakamoto to two bars of melody from Elmer Bernstein.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: As an orchestrator do you usually get a piano score? What is given to you?

It depends. I mean there are some composers, for example I orchestrated for Ryuichi Sakamoto who was a genius. He basically could have done it all himself. He sketched it out and sent, you know these days people send synth demos that you take it from. But then I orchestrated for Elmer Bernstein on the film and he gave me like two bars of melody with no key signature and just said, you know, “Do whatever you like, make it sound good.”
I hope you got paid more for that one.

Well it was nice, you know, when I got to the studio he said, “Well you know what it sounds like, you go and conduct the band and I’ll just sit in the control room.” I love working with him because obviously I mean you know, how can you not love working with Elmer Bernstein?
